editorial.marketOverview: Before the data, QQQ was down 2.89% and SPY 1.95% at 08:01 ET, with chips lagging. The official macro releases now show stronger GDP and persistent core inflation. Cash session has not opened.
editorial.whatChanged: BEA revised third-quarter growth from 3.4% to 4.3% annualized. October headline PCE rose 0.3% monthly versus 0.5% in September, while core remained 0.3%. This changes the policy-risk assessment from pending data to confirmed mixed inflation and stronger growth. No new curated Open Watch events.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Stronger output supports earnings but may reduce urgency for policy relief; flat real consumption in October tempers the growth signal. The pre-release 97% December hike probability cannot be treated as updated. Prior paired curve remains 23.7 bp, not current. No verified post-release SOX, VXN, breadth, yields or oil.
editorial.threeDayPath: Wednesday faces a weak opening setup and repricing of the macro data. Friday's abbreviated session may amplify moves. Monday tests whether semiconductor leadership returns and whether weekend OPEC+ news alters inflation risk.
editorial.bullCase: Headline inflation deceleration and strong output could support a rebound if yields and volatility fall and chip participation improves. This is conditional, not an observed response.
editorial.bearCase: Persistent core inflation and stronger GDP could sustain restrictive policy expectations while tariff and AI valuation risks weigh on chips. A weak opening followed by failed recovery would reinforce the bearish path.
editorial.watchNext: Verify post-release futures, paired Treasury yields and Fed pricing; after the open compare QQQ and SOX, breadth and VXN/VIX. Monitor Beige Book, Friday liquidity and weekend oil policy.
